findings.title: Repair perceived as coercion
findings.claim: At the focus adjective جَبَّارِينَ, a power that has a registered repair-and-reintegration branch is experienced by the speakers through its coercive face, so the inhabitants become a force that freezes the group's action.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier جَبَّارِينَ meets 28:19's explicit جَبَّار/مُصْلِح contrast and 26:130's جَبَّارِينَ in violent striking; those independent wider contacts activate the repair/coercion tension and make pressure, rather than a bare size description, the force that explains the refusal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the speakers' fear does more than describe powerful inhabitants: it turns the name into a socially felt pressure, while the repair possibility remains visible as a contained counter-reading.
findings.containment: The ordinary 'zorba bir halk' floor and the conditional refusal remain recoverable. The repair facet is not asserted as the inhabitants' actual conduct, no height or pride branch is admitted, and the target connection morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The cited cross-run support is trusted but graded weak; the two selected connections provide direct target Arabic while their target morphology is absent, so the repair/coercion relation is retained as a bounded reading rather than a definitive lexical verdict.

branch_activations.carrier: The focus form جَبَّارِينَ carries the registered repair-and-reintegration possibility of the j-b-r root as a bounded semantic branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied 28:19 target directly places جَبَّار beside مُصْلِح, providing an independent repair/coercion contrast.
branch_activations.activation: The focus label meets that repair-versus-coercion contrast at the feared people: the repair branch remains available as semantic potential, but the speakers' description selects the pressure that makes movement unsafe.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The feared power is read as repair-capacity collapsed into domination, which helps explain why the group treats entry as impossible while preserving the plain reference to a mighty people.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that the inhabitants repair anything, that coercion exhausts جَبَّارِينَ, or that the connection target's unprovided morphology settles the branch.

findings.title: Entry is made hostage to exit
findings.claim: The repeated entry and exit construction makes the group's movement conditional on the occupants' departure: agency at the threshold is transferred from the commanded speakers to those they fear.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers repeat دَخَلَ and خَرَجَ across the two sides of the condition; 17:80 supplies a positively directed entry/exit pair, while 9:13 and 9:81 supply wider fear and withdrawal patterns. Their contact changes the utterance from generic reluctance into an outsourced timing rule.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow the refusal as a causal and spatial diagram: 'we enter' is not rejected in the abstract, but postponed until the feared occupants authorize the threshold by leaving.
findings.containment: The primary-floor meaning remains 'we will not enter until they leave.' The wider passages are contextual contrasts and resonance, not claims that this group is identical with every later withdrawing group; no unanchored 5:23 or 5:24 development is imported.

epistemic.reason: The entry-hostage support is legacy_unbound, while the trusted cross-run support independently preserves the focus entry/exit relation. Exact target Arabic is supplied for the selected connections, but target morphology is absent, so the agency inversion is qualified.

findings.title: A refusal answers covenant language with a counter-formula
findings.claim: Against the supplied covenant frame, the speakers' quoted refusal can be heard as a counter-formula: a prior language of fulfilled binding and hearing/obeying is answered by a condition that makes entry depend on circumstances and the occupants' exit.
findings.mechanism: The exact HFT trace frames commitment as completion and binding at 5:1, records hearing and obedience at 5:7, and names undoing the bond at 5:13; the focus speech at 5:22 then proposes terms through its completed plural saying and its لن ... حتى and إن ... فإنا condition. The contact displaces pledged action with safety supplied by others.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can test the refusal against a concrete wider sequence: the issue is not only fear, but whether a self-authored condition replaces the forward movement implied by an earlier bond.
findings.containment: This is an attributed, qualified contextual reading. The packet leaves open a tactical exception rather than definitive repudiation; six HFT branch records have no registered gloss or facet, target morphology is absent, and no unresolved branch is promoted beyond its supplied role.

epistemic.reason: The HFT record supplies exact Arabic anchor coverage and word-index/root roles for 5:1, 5:7, 5:13, and 5:22, but it is legacy_unbound, target morphology is not supplied, and six auxiliary branch records remain unresolved; the tactical-exception alternative stays live.
